Spread and total: the desk's probability sits 14 to 19 points from the no-vig market. The gap comes from a two-game rating sample (SAC 0-2, MEM 2-0). No sourced news found that the market has not priced, so the rule requiring a named, sourced reason for a gap above 8 points is not met.

Margin arithmetic: model.margin -1.1 (home SAC, no home court in the model). Add home court +2.3 gives SAC +1.2. Injury adjustments net to zero: Murray (SAC) and Coward (MEM) are both questionable with no same-day expected-to-play source, and each is taken as a 50/50 with offsetting effects (about -0.5 each). SAC +1.2 gives P(SAC win) = Phi(1.2/12.6) = 0.54; P(SAC cover +3.5) = Phi(4.7/12.6) = 0.65; P(MEM win) = 0.46; P(MEM cover -3.5) = 0.35.

Total arithmetic: model.total 222.3 at model pace 101.7. The two teams' own paces (SAC 102.3, MEM 103.7) average 103.0, so the total scales to 222.3 x 103.0 / 101.7 = 225.1. Injuries not added: SAC's missing bigs (Cardwell, Raynaud, Simmons) have been out since 10-15 to 10-21 and are in the two-game ratings; MEM's Edey (out, ankle, return listed 10-26) does not appear in the payload's MEM game logs, so his absence is assumed to be in the sample too. P(under 234.5) = Phi((234.5 - 225.1) / 18.5) = 0.69. Cross-check: the payload's league averages (ORtg 108.9, pace 104.4) give a league-average game of about 227.4, which gives P(under) = 0.65. Both sit well above the no-vig 0.50, and no sourced news explains a 7-point gap between the line and the league-average total.
